definitions.title: The Integrating Factor Method
definitions.latex: \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \implies \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx}, \quad y(x) = \frac{1}{\mu(x)} \int \mu(x) Q(x) dx
definitions.statement: Any first-order linear differential equation in standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) can be solved by multiplying through by the integrating factor mu(x) = exp(int P(x)dx), collapsing the left side into the product derivative d/dx[mu(x) y].
conditions: P(x) and Q(x) are continuous on interval I
definitions.explanation: Transforms an insoluble equation into an exact total derivative.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Multiply by mu(x) = exp(int P dx) to collapse left side into d/dx[mu * y].
